subject: Physics
description: Charge, Coulomb's law, electric field, capacitance, conductors vs insulators, lightning

questions.stem: TWO LIKE charges placed near each other will:

options.option_text: Attract each other with a strong force
Repel each other with a force given by Coulomb's law
Neither attract nor repel under any circumstance
Move in a circle around their common centre

questions.explanation: Like charges (both positive or both negative) REPEL; unlike charges ATTRACT. Coulomb's law: F = k q₁q₂/r² where k = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C². Force is along the line joining charges; inversely proportional to square of distance. Distractor 1 — opposite of true. Distractor 3 — false; charges always exert force. Distractor 4 — orbital motion would require continuous attraction (like gravity), not the case for like charges.

questions.stem: If the distance between two point charges is DOUBLED, the force between them becomes:

options.option_text: Double the original force value
One-fourth of the original force value
Half of the original force value
One-eighth of the original force value

questions.explanation: Coulomb's law: F ∝ 1/r². If r is doubled (r → 2r), force becomes F/4. Inverse-SQUARE law (same form as gravity). Distractor 1 doubles (would be wrong inverse-linear). Distractor 3 halves. Distractor 4 = 1/8 (wrong cube law).

questions.stem: The SI unit of electric charge is the:

options.option_text: Volt, named after Italian physicist Volta
Coulomb, named after French physicist Coulomb
Ampere, the named SI unit of electric current
Watt, the SI unit of total power output

questions.explanation: Charge — coulomb (C). 1 C is the charge transported by 1 ampere flowing for 1 second. Charge of one electron ≈ −1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; 1 C ≈ 6.24 × 10¹⁸ electrons. Volt = unit of potential difference (V = J/C). Ampere = unit of current (C/s). Watt = unit of power (J/s).

questions.stem: Why is the metal frame of an electrical appliance EARTHED (grounded)?

options.option_text: To make the appliance run faster than usual
To safely conduct away any leaked current to the earth
To shield the appliance from outside lightning strikes
To reduce the internal heating of the appliance motor

questions.explanation: Earthing — connects the metal body to ground via a low-resistance wire. If a live wire accidentally contacts the metal body, the current flows safely to earth instead of through a person who touches the appliance. Trips the fuse / MCB before harm. Three-pin plugs in India: live + neutral + earth. Distractor 1 — false; earthing doesn't affect speed. Distractor 3 — partial truth for outdoor lightning rods, but indoor earthing is for fault current. Distractor 4 — false.

questions.stem: Conductors and insulators differ primarily because conductors:

options.option_text: Lack any internal atomic-level electron structure
Have free electrons that can move under an applied field
Are always heavier than equivalent insulator pieces
Always cool down faster than the surrounding insulator

questions.explanation: Conductors (metals) — outermost electrons are loosely bound, can drift under an applied electric field → carry current. Insulators (rubber, plastic, glass, dry wood) — electrons are tightly bound to atoms; minimal flow. Semiconductors (silicon, germanium) — intermediate conductivity, controllable via doping. Distractor 1 — both have electrons; the difference is mobility. Distractor 3 — weight is unrelated. Distractor 4 — false; conductors usually conduct heat well TOO, but cooling rate depends on many factors.

questions.stem: A capacitor's primary function in an electrical circuit is to:

options.option_text: Generate a steady supply of direct current
Store electrical energy in an electric field temporarily
Convert AC to DC using internal rectifier diodes
Amplify a small voltage signal coming from the source

questions.explanation: Capacitor — two conductors separated by an insulator (dielectric). Stores energy as charge separation: U = ½CV². Capacitance C = Q/V (farads). Used for: smoothing power supplies, blocking DC while passing AC, timing circuits, energy storage in flash bulbs / defibrillators. Distractor 1 = battery / cell role. Distractor 3 = rectifier role. Distractor 4 = transistor / amplifier role.

questions.stem: Lightning rods on tall buildings work primarily by:

options.option_text: Repelling lightning back up into the cloud above
Providing a low-resistance path to safely earth the strike
Producing a counter-current that cancels the lightning
Absorbing the lightning's energy into a internal coil

questions.explanation: Lightning rod — sharp metal point at the highest point of a building, connected by a thick conductor to the ground. When lightning strikes, the rod offers the path of least resistance, conducting the current safely to earth without flowing through the building. Invented by Benjamin Franklin (1752). The 'sharp point' helps initiate corona discharge that ionises the air, often draining the cloud's charge gradually before a sudden strike. Distractor 1 — rods don't repel. Distractor 3 — no counter-current is produced. Distractor 4 — capacitor-style absorption isn't how rods work.
